_comment: Canonical vocabulary for Ultimate Context Engineering, linked into the prose by the shared domain runtime (../shared/domain, repo varasrinivas/course-walkthrough-runtime). Deliberately NOT inside bench/seed/dataset.json: that file's own _contract makes it the single source of truth for the running app, the Spring backend loads it into H2 at every boot, and build-lab.md tells lab authors to draw entities from it — teaching vocabulary does not belong in an app contract, even though @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) on SeedData means an extra key would in fact be tolerated. The cast this glossary refers to (PA-1001..1010, M-2001 Rosa Delgado, procedure 72148) lives there and is not copied here. Rebuild with shared/domain/build.py after course/inject_staged.py or the walkthrough build.
title: Course Glossary
subtitle: Every word this course leans on. Press g from anywhere.

watchlist.skip: ordinary statistics, and the course explains its fresh-session protocol where it matters
covered by Cacheable prefix; the bare word is ordinary English here
used in several ordinary senses — freshness gate, confidence gate, approval gate — each explained where it appears
defined structurally by Five layers rather than as a word on its own
one of the ten auth requests in bench/seed/dataset.json, not vocabulary — the cast is defined there

glossary.short: The app the whole course measures.
glossary.long: A prior-authorization review queue with a Spring backend and a React front end, chosen because it shows its tokens: every call comes back with an itemised receipt. Its data is bench/seed/dataset.json.

glossary.short: The itemised, layer-by-layer token bill returned by every call.
glossary.long: The course's instrument. Read it line by line and each line is a track: system, retrieved, tool, history, user. The five always sum to the input total, and checking that reconciliation is the first thing to do to any token dashboard anyone shows you.

glossary.short: System, retrieved, tool, history, user — the receipt's unit of account.
glossary.long: System is the standing instructions; retrieved is whatever the assembler pulled from the domain; tool is what lookups returned; history is the conversation so far; user is the question itself, routinely the smallest line on the bill.

glossary.short: One strategy, run over the whole question set — one column of the grid.
glossary.long: Ten modes means ten arms. An arm is only ever quoted with its correctness verdict, because an arm that saves tokens and drops a load-bearing fact has not saved anything.

glossary.short: Every arm crossed with every standing question.
glossary.long: The course's whole claim structure: arms down one axis, questions across the other, each cell a token count and a verdict. Nothing is asserted that the grid cannot show.

glossary.short: One of the ten context-assembly strategies the app can switch between.
glossary.long: naive, budgeted, compressed, cached, jit, graph, okf, notes, isolated, routed — the curriculum maps one-to-one onto them, so every idea in the course is a toggle you can flip and measure.

glossary.short: One of the ten fixed questions every arm is graded against.
glossary.long: Q1-Q2 structural, Q3-Q4 canonical, Q5-Q6 logic, Q7-Q8 abstention, Q9-Q10 aggregation. Fixed on purpose: a strategy that only looks good on questions chosen after the fact has not been measured.

glossary.short: The facts an answer must contain to count as correct.
glossary.long: Derived from bench/seed/dataset.json rather than written by hand, so the grader cannot drift away from the data the app is actually serving.

glossary.short: A fact the correct answer depends on. Drop it and the answer is wrong.
glossary.long: The unit the correctness gate is defined in. Compression that keeps the prose and loses one of these reads fine and is worthless.

glossary.short: The verdict on an arm that saved tokens and lost a required fact.
glossary.long: The course's central rule made mechanical: no token number is ever reported without its correctness verdict, and a cheaper wrong answer scores nothing at all.

glossary.short: A check that a compressed context still carries what it claims to.
glossary.long: The last step of the compressed mode's prune, extract-verbatim, abstract sequence — the point at which summarisation stops being a hope and becomes something that can fail loudly.

glossary.short: Answering "I do not know" instead of inventing something.
glossary.long: A gradeable skill, not a failure. Q7 exists to punish confident wrongness: an answer key set with no abstention trap cannot catch fabrication.

glossary.short: Recorded model responses, so every lab runs with no API key.
glossary.long: The default. Live mode is optional depth. It is also what makes the course's numbers reproducible — the same question returns the same bytes on your machine as on the author's.

glossary.short: One recorded response, saved so it can be replayed.
glossary.long: Numbers labelled synthetic-pre-recording came from fixtures. The U02 lab re-earns every one of them, which is the honest way to use a recording: as something you can regenerate, not something you must trust.

glossary.short: Open Knowledge Format — one canonical concept file instead of a document dump.
glossary.long: Also the name of the mode that uses it. Knowledge as Markdown with YAML frontmatter, which is what lets a single small file answer a question that a folder of prose could not. The parent Knowledge Graphs course builds these.

glossary.short: The one agreed version of something, rather than a copy of it.
glossary.long: Used in three senses here, and worth keeping apart: a canonical concept file (the okf mode), the canonical strategy frame (write, select, compress, isolate), and canonical few-shot examples. All three mean the same thing — one authoritative version — applied to different material.

glossary.short: How specific or general a system prompt is pitched.
glossary.long: Too low and it is a brittle script; too high and it is a motivational poster. Altitude is the dial between them, and it is a design decision rather than a matter of taste.

glossary.short: Summarising a long conversation so it keeps fitting the window.
glossary.long: The moment a session's history stops being a transcript and starts being a rewrite — which is exactly when a load-bearing fact can quietly disappear.

glossary.short: The unchanging head of a prompt, which the provider can bill at a discount.
glossary.long: Only unbroken from the start of the prompt, which is why ordering is a cost decision: one moved token can void the whole prefix.

glossary.short: Past a point, adding context makes answers worse rather than better.
glossary.long: Not a capacity limit but an attention one — a window can rot well below its stated size, so 'it fits' is never the same as 'it helps'.

glossary.short: Attention degrades as the window fills, so every low-signal token taxes the high-signal ones.
glossary.long: The reason context engineering is a budgeting discipline rather than a packing one.

glossary.short: Where a number came from, recorded next to it.
glossary.long: Every figure in this course states its conditions, and a citation that does not resolve fails the build. A measurement whose origin you cannot check is a claim.

glossary.short: A separate call with its own clean window, whose summary comes back.
glossary.long: How the isolated mode works: the messy gathering happens somewhere the main window never sees, and only a small answer crosses back.

glossary.short: A health insurer's approval, required before certain treatment is given.
glossary.long: The domain MedFlow Copilot works in. A reviewer weighs a request against the plan's criteria and approves, denies, or asks for more; that judgement is what the app assembles context for.

glossary.short: A bracketed tag pointing at the source a claim rests on.
glossary.long: [ANTHROPIC-CE], [LC-WSCI], [ROT-LIT], [PARENT-KG] and [PARENT-KIT] all resolve in docs/canon.md. They exist so a reader can check a claim against the work it came from rather than taking the course's word for it.
